chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abd al-Rahman said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, then it became clear to him after he had consummated the marriage with her that she had an absent husband. He left her, then the husband arrived and either divorced her or died. Should the man who married her (and did not know she had a husband) marry her again after this? He said: 'I do not like for him to marry her until she marries another husband.' The reason in this report is a type of dislike (karahah). For that reason he said 'and I do not like for him to marry her,' and he did not say 'and it is not permissible.' The reason in the two reports, in my view, is that it was permissible for him to marry her if the woman did not intend (by choice) the marriage while knowing that her husband was still alive as he was; rather, he had been absent from her, so news of him was brought to her, or divorce from him reached her. Because if she had intended that while knowing the state of the husband, she would be a fornicator (zaniyah). And if she is a fornicator, it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with her ever, because whoever marries a woman with a husband (dhat ba'l) is not permissible for her ever, as we explained in our Great Book. And that which indicates that whenever she intends that while knowing the state of the husband, she is a fornicator.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He consummated the marriage with her
key_terms.زَانِيَة: Fornicator (specifically a woman with a living husband)
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَة: Dislike (a legal ruling less severe than prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Can a man remarry a woman if her previous husband was absent and later divorced her or died?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Isfabar, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between mere dislike (karahah) and impermissibility (haram) regarding a man remarrying a woman whose absent husband was discovered after consummation. The ruling hinges on whether the woman knowingly concealed her existing marriage; if she did, she is considered a fornicator (zaniyah) and becomes permanently prohibited to him, whereas if she was unaware or the husband was absent, the marriage remains valid.
